user.title: Measurement sources
user.description: Tell WattSplit what measures energy in the home. Sensors are grouped by what they measure, and you can add as many as you have: several inverters, several meters, per-phase sensors. You need at least one sensor that shows consumption or grid power.

data.load_entities: Load sensors (per phase, circuit or whole house)
data.invert_grid: Grid meters report export as positive

data_description.house_entity: A ready-made total consumption sensor. If set, it is used as the whole-home value.
data_description.grid_entity: Net power at the connection to the utility: positive when importing, negative when exporting.
data_description.load_entities: Power consumed on a phase, a circuit or the whole house, whatever supplies it. Each one is watched separately, so a quiet circuit shows small appliances.
data_description.generation_entities: Anything that produces power for the house. Used as evidence of where an appliance gets its power, never searched for loads.
data_description.battery_entity: Positive when the battery feeds the house, negative when charging.

error.no_source: Pick at least one house, grid or load sensor.

user.title: Add appliance
user.description: Link an on/off entity, a power sensor, both, or neither. With neither, WattSplit infers the appliance from steps in the house signal.

data_description.state_entity: Optional. Lets WattSplit learn the appliance's power from when it switches.
data_description.power_entity: Optional. If the appliance already has a power sensor, WattSplit only uses it to subtract it from the house signal.
data_description.power_mode: Known: use the power below. Prior: use it as a hint and refine it. Learn: declare nothing. Pinned: a learned value you froze.
data_description.power_levels: One value, or several separated by commas (for example 3200, 5500 for a two-stage shower).
data_description.energy_entity: The appliance's own cumulative energy sensor (Wh or kWh). A clean measurement that WattSplit uses as a starting point and a cross-check: energy between updates divided by the time the appliance was on. It may update only once an hour; that is enough.

init.title: WattSplit options
init.description: Tell WattSplit what measures energy in the home. Sensors are grouped by what they measure, and you can add as many as you have: several inverters, several meters, per-phase sensors. You need at least one sensor that shows consumption or grid power.

data.load_entities: Load sensors (per phase, circuit or whole house)
data.invert_grid: Grid meters report export as positive
data.export_energy: Add estimates to the Energy dashboard (once)

data_description.house_entity: A ready-made total consumption sensor. If set, it is used as the whole-home value.
data_description.grid_entity: Net power at the connection to the utility: positive when importing, negative when exporting.
data_description.load_entities: Power consumed on a phase, a circuit or the whole house, whatever supplies it. Each one is watched separately, so a quiet circuit shows small appliances.
data_description.generation_entities: Anything that produces power for the house. Used as evidence of where an appliance gets its power, never searched for loads.
data_description.battery_entity: Positive when the battery feeds the house, negative when charging.
data_description.evidence: Sensors that may carry part of an appliance's power, such as a solar inverter or a battery. Each one is checked against each appliance's on/off changes and counts only if it clearly follows them; its share is then added. They are never searched for loads, so a passing cloud is not mistaken for one. Leave empty to use the generation and battery sensors above when detection runs on the grid signal.
data_description.sample_interval: How often the engine looks at its inputs. How long it averages is set automatically from how often each sensor actually reports.
data_description.min_step_w: A floor. Each channel raises it automatically to clear its own noise.
data_description.import_energy: Fills empty source lists with the dashboard's grid, solar and battery power sensors, and adds an appliance for each of its individual devices (with its on/off entity and energy counter guessed from the same device). Devices already added are left alone.
data_description.export_energy: Adds the estimated energy of appliances that have no energy counter of their own (a pool pump, a shower...) as individual devices of the Energy dashboard, so they stop being part of its 'untracked consumption'. Appliances that already have a counter are left alone and nothing is removed.
